title: Paying for Orders with Gift Cards & Store Credit
content:
Several Gift Cards & Store Credit instruments can pay one order. They are drawn in the tender capture priority of Online Orders, with no more instruments of each type on the order than the most that type allows on one order.

## Conditions of spending

1. An instrument is spent only while it is in status active, and, for an expiring instrument, only on or before its expiry date. A Bonus Gift Card cannot be spent before its valid-from date. These conditions are read from the instrument's own record in the system, not from what the customer says about it.
2. A Bonus Gift Card applies only when the order's merchandise subtotal after discounts reaches the Bonus Gift Card's minimum merchandise subtotal.
3. An instrument that does not pay shipping fees pays merchandise only; the remainder falls to the next tender.
4. No instrument can pay for a gift card line.
5. A bearer card used online needs its PIN.
6. Value spent never exceeds the balance; there is no negative balance.
7. No instrument can pay a pre-order deposit; deposits are taken by card under the Pre-Orders & Back-Orders terms.

## Boundary days (hypothetical dates)

| Instrument and day of spending | Can it be spent? |
|---|---|
| Active Goodwill Credit, on its expiry date | Yes — on or before the expiry date |
| The same Goodwill Credit, on the day after its expiry date | No |
| Active Bonus Gift Card, on its valid-from date | Yes |
| Bonus Gift Card, on the day before its valid-from date | No |
| Return Store Credit in status locked, any day | No — only an active instrument is spent |

## Points of judgement

- **Shipping on a mixed basket (hypothetical):** a Marlowe Rewards Note does not pay shipping fees, so on an order of 80.00 merchandise and 6.95 shipping, a note can pay at most the 80.00 of merchandise, and the 6.95 falls to the next tender.
- **Gift card lines:** an order containing a Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card line cannot use any stored-value instrument for that line.
- **Balance limit:** an instrument holding 12.40 pays at most 12.40 of an order; the balance never goes below zero.
